_doc: PROPOSAL (task M3-01), not game data: the pacing simulator's redesign model reads this folder, the game does not. It follows the owner's economy rules in design spec section 14: small numbers, one job per currency (cubes for Lumi's tracks, base levels and builds; Parts for robots, repairs and rig modules; seeds for planting), scarce Parts at the start, a crew of about 12. Global numbers for the Planet 1 redesign. All times are BOT seconds unless a field says otherwise; a new player is bot_to_player times slower at actions (growth timers are real time for both). planet_id: the planet whose unchanged tables are read through Planets (litter value mix from 'pollution', perfect-press multiplier from 'player'). target_bot_min: the bot's target time to the ending and the accepted range. start.delay_s: seconds from gaining control to the first sweep. hand: baler_unlock = the id that turns loose tipping into pressing bales; base_rate = units of litter swept a second before any bonus; capacity = chest size in units; tip_s = one walk to the bin and back to tip a loose load; press_s = pressing one bale; carry_s = one walk to the scale with a stack of carry_stack bales; loose_mult = payout multiplier for loose trash tipped in the bin (the current game pays 1.3; the proposal is 1.0 so a bale always wins); shop_s = seconds one purchase costs at the bench. mastery: level L needs mastery_level1_units (per kind, pollution.json) x growth^(L-1) units of that kind cleared by hand in total; hand_bonus_per_level is Lumi's rate bonus per level; unlock = the id that starts mastery. surge: unlock id; charge_s = seconds of hand work (sweeping, pressing, tending) for a full charge; duration_s and mult = the burst; wave = from the wave unlock on, a release also adds burst_pts growth points to `hexes` hexes of the district; linked = from that unlock on, crew in Lumi's district work at crew_mult during a Surge.
